public_comment.topic: Asked the school committee to give formal feedback on master plan recommendations that pertain to the schools.

votes.motion: Motion to accept, with gratitude, the donation check from Hanford/Hannerford Health Schools to the high school gift account.
Motion to accept the second, unallocated donation from Hanford Alps.
Motion to raise the daily substitute teacher rate and the long-term substitute rates as recommended.
Motion to approve the revised FY27 capital plan recommendations as described in the document.
Motion to waive the second reading and treat it as the second reading for policies 5201.03 (Middle School Pathways) and 5204.01 (Competency Determination).

budget_items.what_was_said: A check donation to the high school gift account was accepted with a roll-call vote.
A second donation with no specific account allocation was accepted; it will go into the Turkey Hill field trip account.
The business manager reported the current FY25 available budget/surplus figure, noting it will likely go down once the town closes its books.
Net school spending was cited as the base figure against which a 2% special education reserve contribution would be calculated.
Members discussed how much could have been set aside for special education costs had the new reserve fund existed a year earlier.

budget_items.topic: Hypothetical reduced surplus if reserve had existed
budget_items.what_was_said: Funding the hypothetical special-education reserve would have left a much smaller year-end surplus, members said.
This line was cited to town meeting as having more than tripled since 2023, driving the need for a reserve fund.
Members said individual out-of-district or collaborative placements are getting very expensive and vary widely in cost.
The business manager located pupil transportation figures on schedule 19, separating regular-day and special-education transportation costs.

budget_items.topic: Cost of adding one student requiring a transport van
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff said adding a single student needing a van and monitor, if not regionalized, would have to come out of the current year's budget.
The business manager compared Lunenburg's substitute rate to five neighboring districts, finding Lunenburg the lowest payer in the region.
The substitute line was reported as far less spent than the prior year, which staff attributed to difficulty attracting substitutes rather than savings.
The business manager recommended raising the daily and long-term substitute rates to align with the regional average; the committee later approved this.
The business manager priced a seven-passenger van meeting new legal requirements, citing an existing earmark requiring a minimum spend on such vans.
The superintendent listed health insurance, transportation, and supply cost increases plus contractual salary raises as the main FY27 cost drivers.

budget_items.topic: FY27 preliminary budget total vs FY26
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager gave the preliminary FY27 total against the current FY26 budget, an increase attributed largely to new positions and fixed costs.
The business manager said he would confirm projected utility increases with the provider and noted the district is currently running over its electricity line.

budget_items.topic: Health insurance carried in school budget
budget_items.what_was_said: A member argued the school budget's percentage increase looks larger than other departments' because the school committee alone carries its full health insurance cost in its budget.

budget_items.topic: Central office restructuring: half-time data manager
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed adding a half-time clerical data manager position to support the business office, to be included in the FY27 budget presentation.

budget_items.topic: FY27 budget percent increase with/without clerical position
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager gave slightly different overall FY27 percentage increases depending on whether the new clerical position is included.

transfers.description: Prior-year transfer into the substitute teacher pay line

decisions.decision: The superintendent and business manager will revise the draft public statement on the FY25 surplus with member feedback for possible release/approval at the next meeting.
Committee will wait for more information from the superintendent before deciding whether to submit an MSBA statement of interest for Turkey Hill this cycle.

Superintendent will bring the central office restructuring (moving a staff member to accounts payable, adding a half-time data manager) to the Monday tri-board presentation without a formal committee vote.
The cashless athletics campus policy was returned to the policy subcommittee rather than proceeding to a second reading.
Committee asked the policy subcommittee to also draft a formal cash-handling policy covering field trips, the snack shack, and ticket sales.
Feedback on the advertising policy (restricting political party/lobbyist advertising) was referred back to the policy subcommittee.

minutes.headline: Superintendent's preliminary FY27 budget restores paraprofessional and intervention positions cut in prior years.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed FY25 year-end finances and a growing surplus, accepted donations, and voted to raise substitute teacher pay to match regional rates. It revised the FY27 capital plan, discussed pursuing state building assistance for Turkey Hill Elementary, and heard the superintendent's preliminary FY27 budget memo, which restores several paraprofessional, interventionist, and other positions cut in recent years. A proposed cashless athletics-campus policy was sent back to the policy subcommittee after resident feedback, and a member raised concern that the school budget's health insurance line makes its year-over-year increase look larger than other town departments'.

what_happened.line: The superintendent's preliminary FY27 budget memo restores paraprofessional, interventionist and other positions cut in recent years.
The committee voted to raise substitute teacher pay after finding Lunenburg paid the least of five neighboring districts.
The committee voted to approve a revised FY27 capital plan and continued weighing whether to seek state building assistance for Turkey Hill Elementary.
A proposed cashless athletics-campus payment policy was sent back to the policy subcommittee after resident feedback.
A member said the school budget's health insurance line makes its year-over-year increase look larger than other town departments'.

why_it_matters: The preliminary FY27 memo signals a shift from recent cuts and will move through the district's budget process toward a town meeting vote.
Raising substitute pay changes a line item residents will see in the FY27 budget and affects staffing coverage in classrooms.
How the health insurance line is presented can shape comparisons between the school budget's growth and the town's other departments.
